summary.source: UCI ServiceNow incident log (CC BY 4.0), a real company's IT service desk

cards.title: Incidents that wait on someone outside the team miss their SLA 2.4× as often
cards.recommendation: Waiting for the user is 31% of all open time. Remind the user automatically and close or pause stale waits.
cards.not_explained_by: measured on the real event log (learning period)

cards.title: 24% of all open time is spent waiting for someone to pick the incident up
cards.recommendation: Staff the teams where incidents queue longest at the hours they arrive (see next week's forecast).
cards.not_explained_by: measured on the real event log (learning period)

cards.title: Category 26: 57% of incidents are passed between teams
cards.comparison_text: Category 26 incidents that stayed with one team
cards.recommendation: Agree a single owning team for Category 26, or route it there directly when OpsLens is sure.
cards.not_explained_by: measured on the real event log (learning period)

routing.note: The final team is not always the 'right' one: many incidents go to the front-line desk (Group 70) by design. OpsLens only suggests a team when it is at least this sure.

fasttrack.question: If the desk can fast-track 10%, 20% or 30% of each day's new incidents at their 1-hour mark, whose pick saves more missed deadlines?
fasttrack.assumption: A log cannot be replayed. We assume a fast-tracked incident is picked up the moment its first hour ends and that everything after the pickup happens exactly as it really did.

left_out.why: The company flags almost every Critical or High incident as missed, however fast it was resolved, so no deadline rule can score them. A desk fast-tracks them anyway; they are left out of the benchmark (and of every picker's budget).

pickup.definition: Pickup = the first event in a state other than New. New straight to Resolved: no pickup recorded, the New time includes the fix, so no wait is counted (understates savings).

pickers.label: Logistic regression, same features as OpsLens

rule.text: OpsLens's pick is better only if it saves more misses than the best other picker at the 20% budget, with a 95% CI (whole test weeks resampled) excluding 0.

impact.assumption: A log cannot be replayed. We assume a fast-tracked incident is picked up the moment its first hour ends and that everything after the pickup happens exactly as it really did.

productivity.text: No claim. Fast-tracking moves the same work earlier; the log cannot show whether agents would close more incidents per hour.

money.why: No cost per missed deadline exists for this desk (config/impact.yaml is not part of the project), and we do not invent one.

replication.rule: Found on the learning months; replicates only if the gap keeps its sign on the test months with a 95% CI (whole test weeks resampled) excluding 0.

forecast_candidates.note: WAPE = sum of |forecast - actual| / sum of actual over team-days. Chosen on the check weeks only.

alerts.definition: Overloaded team-day = more new incidents than the team usually closes in a day (median of the 4 weeks before the test period). Alerts are made a week ahead.

labels.every_weekday: Calendar rule: alert on every weekday
